summary: The narrowed apparent-mask-width claim preserves unusual mutant morphology, does not optimize toward WT width, avoids widest-plane selection, and exposes one routine width measurement.

evidence: sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py keeps short, long, wide, low-ratio, and tortuous cases as morphology warnings rather than comparative technical failures.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:5551 selects largest filled-mask area, then support, then Z; tests verify the widest plane is not selected merely for being widest.
Routine documentation describes apparent mask width and disclaims PSF-corrected physical diameter.

limitations: The learned boundary can be thicker than the visible bright signal.
The threshold diagnostic includes only one retained specimen from each group.
recommended_follow_up: Use independent specimens for group inference and retain the apparent-width qualifier.
